QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_29

question.text: What is the purpose of the Extreme Loss Margin (ELM) in IRD risk management?

answer.text: To act as an additional margin charged in addition to the initial margin for open positions
To replace SPAN margin during periods of extreme volatility
To fund the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund
To cover operational risk of the clearing corporation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 251-252 of the NISM Series IV workbook, upfront initial margin and ELM are charged for open positions. Page 256 states ELM is charged in addition to initial margins, with product-specific rates prescribed. The Trap: ELM does not replace SPAN initial margin; it is charged in addition to it. ELM is a margin levied on members, not a contribution to the SGF, and it addresses market risk rather than operational risk of the clearing corporation. Note: Source-backed rule from pages 251-253 and 256 of Series IV: SPAN computes the initial margin and ELM is layered on top of it as an additional margin for open positions.
